subject: Art and Culture
sub_topic: Types of stupas — relic, commemorative, votive

concepts.name: Relic Stupas: Definition and Doctrinal Significance
key_dimensions: Distinction between corporeal relics (sarira) vs. objects used by Buddha
Eight original stupas built over Buddha's ashes after Mahaparinirvana
Concept of dhatu-garbha (relic chamber) and its architectural placement
Ashoka's redistribution of relics and creation of 84,000 stupas legend

concepts.name: Major Relic Stupas in India: Identification and Features
key_dimensions: Sanchi Stupa as the most prominent relic stupa example
Piprahwa stupa and its controversial identification as Kapilavastu relic site
Ratnagiri stupa complex in Odisha and relic casket discoveries
Distinction from commemorative stupas at same sites (e.g., Sanchi Stupa 2 vs. Stupa 1)

concepts.name: Commemorative Stupas: Purpose and Locations
key_dimensions: Built at sites of significant events in Buddha's life (birth, enlightenment, first sermon, death)
Eight great places of pilgrimage (Ashtamahapratiharya) and their stupas
Difference from relic stupas: no physical remains, only symbolic significance
Examples: Sarnath (first sermon), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment), Kushinagar (parinirvana)

concepts.name: Votive Stupas: Scale, Purpose and Distribution
key_dimensions: Miniature stupas created as offerings by devotees or monks
Found in large numbers at monastery sites (Nalanda, Taxila, Ratnagiri)
Made of terracotta, stone, or metal; often contain miniature relics or inscriptions
Distinction from main stupas: personal devotional objects vs. community worship centers

concepts.name: Architectural Differences Across Stupa Types
key_dimensions: Size hierarchy: relic stupas (largest) > commemorative > votive (smallest)
Relic chamber presence: mandatory in relic stupas, absent in commemorative
Circumambulation path (pradakshina patha): elaborate in relic/commemorative, minimal in votive
Decorative elements: most elaborate in commemorative stupas at pilgrimage sites

concepts.name: Relic Caskets and Deposit Systems
key_dimensions: Multi-layered casket system (stone > crystal > gold > actual relic)
Inscriptions on caskets identifying donors and relic type
Archaeological discoveries: Bhattiprolu, Piprahwa, Taxila casket finds
Difference between authentic relics and symbolic substitutes (pratirupa-sarira)

concepts.name: The Eight Great Stupas Tradition
key_dimensions: Canonical list of eight events commemorated by stupas
Geographic spread across ancient India (modern India, Nepal, Pakistan)
Variations in Theravada vs. Mahayana traditions regarding the eight sites
UPSC trap: confusion between eight relic stupas (Ashoka's distribution) vs. eight commemorative stupas

concepts.name: Ashoka's Role in Stupa Typology
key_dimensions: Opening of seven original stupas and redistribution of relics
Construction of both relic stupas (84,000 legend) and commemorative pillars
Inscriptional evidence of Ashoka's stupa enlargements (Nigali Sagar inscription)
Distinction between Ashokan stupas and pre-Ashokan stupas (archaeological evidence)

concepts.name: Votive Stupas: Inscriptional Evidence
key_dimensions: Donor inscriptions revealing social composition (monks, nuns, laity, guilds)
Merit-making (punya) as primary motivation for votive stupa creation
Regional language variations in votive inscriptions (Prakrit, Sanskrit, local scripts)
Dating evidence from paleography and associated coins

concepts.name: Stupa Types and Sectarian Differences
key_dimensions: Theravada emphasis on relic stupas as primary worship objects
Mahayana expansion of commemorative stupas for Bodhisattvas and teachers
Vajrayana introduction of dharani stupas (containing sacred texts)
Architectural variations: hemispherical (Theravada) vs. tower-like (Mahayana)

concepts.name: Archaeological Identification Challenges
key_dimensions: Difficulty distinguishing commemorative from relic stupas without excavation
Later additions of relics to originally commemorative stupas
Votive stupas sometimes containing relics, blurring classifications
UPSC trap: assuming all large stupas are relic stupas

concepts.name: Stupa Multiplication and Fragmentation of Relics
key_dimensions: Buddhist doctrine allowing infinite division of relics without diminution of power
Contrast with Hindu pratishtha concepts of consecration
Historical accounts of relic distribution (Ashokavadana, Mahaparinibbana Sutta)
Implications for stupa proliferation across Buddhist world

concepts.name: Commemorative Stupas at Jataka Sites
key_dimensions: Stupas built at locations of Buddha's previous birth stories
Examples: Sanchi Stupa 2 reliefs depicting Jataka tales
Distinction from main biographical event stupas
Regional variations in which Jatakas were commemorated architecturally

concepts.name: Votive Tablets vs. Votive Stupas
key_dimensions: Votive tablets (clay plaques) as alternative devotional objects
Functional overlap: both serve merit-making purposes
Archaeological contexts: tablets more portable, stupas fixed installations
UPSC trap: confusing votive stupas with votive tablets in site descriptions

concepts.name: Evolution of Stupa Types Over Time
key_dimensions: Early period (3rd century BCE-1st century CE): dominance of relic stupas
Middle period (1st-7th century CE): proliferation of commemorative stupas
Late period (7th-12th century CE): increase in votive stupas at monastery sites
Correlation with changing Buddhist practices and patronage patterns

concepts.name: Regional Variations in Stupa Classification
key_dimensions: Gandhara: emphasis on narrative relief stupas (commemorative function)
Deccan: large relic stupas with elaborate gateways (Sanchi, Amaravati)
Eastern India: monastery-centered votive stupa clusters (Nalanda, Ratnagiri)
Sri Lanka: preservation of tooth relic tradition (Dalada Maligawa)

concepts.name: Non-Buddhist Influences on Stupa Typology
key_dimensions: Pre-Buddhist burial mounds (megaliths) and their influence on relic stupas
Vedic sacrificial mounds and structural similarities
Jain stupa traditions and cross-influences
UPSC relevance: questions on syncretic architectural features

concepts.name: Textual Sources on Stupa Classification
key_dimensions: Mahaparinibbana Sutta on treatment of Buddha's relics
Ashokavadana on relic redistribution narrative
Chinese pilgrims' accounts (Fa-Hien, Xuanzang) describing stupa types
Later texts like Kriyasamgraha codifying stupa construction rules

concepts.name: Contemporary Stupa Construction and Type Continuity
key_dimensions: Modern relic stupas: Deekshabhoomi (Nagpur) containing Ambedkar's conversion site
Commemorative stupas: Dhamek Stupa renovations at Sarnath
Votive stupa tradition in Tibetan Buddhism (tsa-tsas)
UPSC relevance: linking ancient typology to living traditions

concepts.name: Stupa Types and Pilgrimage Economics
key_dimensions: Relic stupas as major pilgrimage destinations generating economic activity
Commemorative stupas creating sacred geography and pilgrimage circuits
Votive stupas as evidence of monastic economy and patronage networks
Archaeological evidence of trade routes and stupa locations
